title: changenote configuration
description: Packages managed by changenote. Paths and version files are also checked by the CLI.

$schema.description: Schema reference for editors. The CLI does not fetch or validate this reference.

changed_file_patterns.description: Package-relative check paths. Include matches minus all leading-! exclusions. Omission includes every package path.

base_branch.description: Local Git comparison ref for check when --since is omitted. Does not select release Action branches.

ignore.description: Explicit configured packages whose pending notes are retained instead of released. Fixed groups must be paused in full.

linked.description: Disjoint explicit-name groups that share a version baseline without activating inactive members.

fixed.description: Groups of names or * and ? patterns. Each must resolve to at least two distinct disjoint packages; checked by the CLI.

changelog.description: Optional ordered sections. Without this setting, notes are grouped by SemVer bump.

title.description: Nonempty trimmed heading without control characters or an initial SemVer version. Titles must be unique; Other Changes is reserved. The CLI checks these rules.

types.description: Note types assigned to this section. A type can occur only once across all sections; the CLI checks this rule.

path.description: Package directory relative to the repository root. Parent components are not allowed.

version_file.description: Version file relative to the package directory. Use VERSION, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, or package.json. Parent components are not allowed.

version_outputs.description: Additional version files relative to the package directory. Each must match the primary version. Parent components, symlinks, and overlapping output paths are not allowed; the CLI checks these rules.

tag_prefix.description: Literal prefix before the full release version, for example sdk/v. The CLI validates the complete Git tag and rejects duplicate planned tags. Without this field, the default tag format is unchanged.
